facts.text: A game engine is the software core of a video game that draws three-dimensional worlds, moves objects with simple physics and runs in real time; many sensor simulators are built on a game engine.
facts.quote: A game engine is the software core of a video game, which draws three-dimensional worlds, moves objects with simple physics and runs in real time, and many sensor simulators are built on one.

facts.text: Writing software that renders a realistic world at 30 or 60 frames per second is enormously expensive, which led the games industry to create reusable engines.
facts.quote: Writing a program that renders a realistic world at 30 or 60 frames per second is enormously expensive, so the games industry created reusable engines.

facts.text: Unreal Engine and Unity are the two best-known game engines.

facts.text: A simulator vendor or research team can add machine models, sensor models and a scenario interface to a game engine to obtain a visual world without writing a renderer.
